architecture: No source/reference identity in Product-facing code or tests
No duplicate document vault or scheduler runtime
Bounded domain interfaces and migration adapters
platform: iOS simulator build/tests before Product v1
acceptance.release_gate: No release candidate until all critical module acceptance criteria and security/license gates pass.

behavioral_targets.target: Stable live outline, reliable capture, direct-manipulation four-corner crop with precision assist, correct perspective output and reversible enhancement.
Continuous multipage capture with durable per-page original, geometry, rotation, enhancement recipe, OCR state and order.
OCR occurs on final rectified content; raw, normalized and user-corrected text are distinguishable; structured fields require confidence and user verification.
Document payload confidentiality and integrity survive save, edit, export, backup, restore and migration; sensitive temporary files are lifecycle-bounded.
Repeat schedules and completion history produce deterministic due-state across timezone, reboot and clock-change scenarios.
Only one scheduling transport is active; document expiry and activity reminders remain semantically owned by their domains.
A single local-first search experience returns authorized results across all domains while data ownership remains separated.
Crop/filter/annotation/page operations preserve originals or explicit edit recipes until a deliberately destructive export is requested.
Core scan, vault, activity, reminder and local-search workflows function without remote accounts or network services.
Shared business rules are behaviorally consistent on Android and iOS; camera, OCR, biometric, file and notification integrations use replaceable native adapters.

modules.purpose: Live camera capture, stable page detection, manual four-corner correction, perspective rectification, non-destructive enhancement, batch sessions and import.
Encrypted document/page storage, structured metadata, people/collections, expiry semantics, favorites, lifecycle, audit and secure sharing.
Post-rectification OCR, searchable normalized text, document classification, confidence-aware structured fields and explicit user verification.
Multipage PDF composition/import/editing, reorder/rotate/merge/split/compress, annotation, signatures, watermarking and verified redaction exports.
Recurring activities, completion history, due/overdue state, flexible schedules, archive/restore and deterministic next-due calculation.
Things, places and relationships with typed links to activities and documents without collapsing domain stores.
Single notification/scheduling transport for activity reminders and document-expiry alerts with boot/time/timezone reconciliation.
One query surface over documents, activities, things and places plus local-first natural-language parsing and voice entry where platform capability permits.
Versioned integrity-checked backup coordinator with encrypted document payload preservation, domain adapters, export/import and optional isolated sync.
Product-wide lock policy, secure key management, biometric/PIN adapters, minimal permissions, secure temporary-file lifecycle, privacy audit and offline-first defaults.
Thin configurations over the shared capture pipeline for identity cards, receipts/invoices, books/two-page spreads, QR/barcode, long/large pages and stitching; no separate monolithic scanner engines.

product_engine_candidates.reason: Matches the locked architecture preference and permits shared scheduling/domain rules while keeping native adapters replaceable.
Current Android source/package already demonstrates an Android camera/document processing path; production acceptance still requires corpus benchmarks.

product_engine_candidates.candidate: ML Kit behind an OCR interface
product_engine_candidates.reason: Current compiled baseline contains the expected OCR pipeline; provider remains replaceable.

product_engine_candidates.candidate: Native Apple camera/vision adapters behind shared contracts
product_engine_candidates.reason: No iOS runner/device proof exists in the current Foundry environment.

product_engine_candidates.candidate: Domain-separated repositories with platform database adapters
product_engine_candidates.reason: Keep separate initial stores and migration boundaries; concrete cross-platform database engine must pass build/migration probes before lock.

product_engine_candidates.candidate: Platform secure keystore/keychain adapters + product-owned envelope format
product_engine_candidates.reason: Do not weaken existing document encryption; exact cross-platform cryptographic storage implementation is not locked pre-probe.

product_thesis: A privacy-first personal document and life-maintenance workspace that combines high-quality document capture and secure document storage with recurring activity tracking, reminders, a personal memory graph, and federated local search. Core workflows remain useful offline; optional network services are isolated and opt-in.

shared_core_contracts.contract: Typed domain + stable opaque ID; cross-domain relationships never depend on foreign database rows.
Domain-owned indexed results expose normalized title/snippet/type/score/action without leaking persistence internals.
Domain supplies stable event ID, trigger policy, timezone semantics and user intent; scheduler owns transport/reconciliation only.
Encrypted payload API separates metadata from ciphertext and supports atomic writes, integrity verification and migration.
Each domain emits/restores versioned records through a coordinator with integrity manifest and rollback-safe migration.
Append-only local event bus for cross-domain updates such as completion, expiry, document change and relationship change.

uncertainties: Ordinary dynamic comparison against the behavioral reference is currently blocked by the available secure execution environment; no dynamic-parity claim is made.
iOS camera/OCR/notification and secure-storage adapters require pre-implementation platform feasibility probes before their engines are locked.
The concrete cross-platform database engine is intentionally not locked until migration/build probes demonstrate compatibility with the domain-separated persistence strategy.

Advanced restoration, book dewarp, long-page stitching and office-conversion capabilities are scope candidates whose engines must pass objective feasibility/quality gates before becoming critical dependencies.
